title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
title_zh: TuringSpace：用交互式验证码检验行动中的空间智能
abstract_en: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same? CAPTCHAs offer a natural test, since humans solve them through this very loop, clicking and dragging on the screen and adjusting after each result. Yet existing CAPTCHA benchmarks are largely solved and rarely spatial, while spatial benchmarks rarely require action. We therefore present TuringSpace, a synthetic web environment of 125 interactive CAPTCHAs that span five spatial abilities and must be solved through clicks and drags on the screen. Every task is a program that generates new instances with a checker and an oracle, so the tasks also form a scalable training gym. Humans solve 94.1% of the tasks, whereas the best model, GPT-6 Astra, still fails 25.9% of them, and the best open-weight model, Kimi K3, fails 68.0%. Our further analysis shows that most failures come from misreading the screenshot, and that model reasoning rarely corrects a wrong belief but hallucinates evidence to defend it. To test whether such spatial abilities can be learned, we fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B on this gym. Its success rate rises from 1.6% to 33.1%, above Kimi K3, and it improves on all seven out-of-distribution benchmarks, including a 9.9-point gain on the real-world indoor videos of VSI-Bench. These results show that grounding spatial intelligence in screen actions exposes what MLLMs lack and offers a scalable way to teach it, with gains that transfer to real-world scenes. We will release TuringSpace to support further study.
abstract_zh: 人类能从二维画面推断三维布局，预测动作会如何改变场景，并根据反馈修正判断。为检验多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）能否完成同样的闭环，论文提出 TuringSpace：一个包含 125 项交互式验证码（CAPTCHA）任务的合成网页环境，覆盖五类空间能力，要求模型通过屏幕点击和拖拽完成任务。每项任务都能程序化生成新实例，并配有结果检查器（checker）和参考求解器（oracle），既可用于评测，也可用于规模化训练。人类的任务成功率为 94.1%，表现最好的 GPT-6 Astra 仍有 25.9% 的任务失败，最佳开放权重模型 Kimi K3 的失败率则为 68.0%。误差分析显示，多数失败源于误读截图；推理很少纠正错误判断，反而常编造证据为其辩护。在该环境中微调后，Qwen3.5-9B 的成功率从 1.6% 升至 33.1%，超过 Kimi K3，并在全部七项分布外基准上取得提升，其中在包含真实室内视频的 VSI-Bench 上提升了 9.9 个百分点。
key_points_zh: TuringSpace 用 125 项覆盖五类空间能力的任务，评测模型能否通过点击、拖拽和观察反馈来修正判断，而非只回答静态图像问题。
人类成功率为 94.1%，GPT-6 Astra 和 Kimi K3 分别为 74.1% 和 32.0%。
多数失败源于误读截图；模型的推理往往为错误判断编造证据，而不是利用反馈纠错。
任务实例可程序化生成并自动判定。微调后，Qwen3.5-9B 的成功率从 1.6% 升至 33.1%，且在七项分布外基准上均有提升。
